definition: A decent and customary mental attitude in the presence of wealth or power.
example: He greeted the board with appropriate abasement—which is to say, he smiled until it hurt.

definition: A statement or belief manifestly inconsistent with one's own opinion.
example: Your proposal is an absurdity; mine is a bold vision.

definition: The death of endeavor and the birth of disgust.
example: Every great achievement carries within it the seed of its own ennui.

definition: A person whom we know well enough to borrow from, but not well enough to lend to.
example: He was a dear acquaintance—close enough to ask favors, too distant to refuse them.

definition: Our polite recognition of another's resemblance to ourselves.
example: She admired his taste tremendously—it was, after all, identical to her own.

definition: The union of two thieves who have their hands so deeply inserted in each other's pockets that they cannot separately plunder a third.
example: Their strategic alliance was celebrated with champagne and mutual suspicion.

definition: In bad company.
example: He preferred to be alone—the only company he reliably found intolerable.

definition: An overmastering desire to be vilified by enemies while living and made ridiculous by friends when dead.
example: His ambition was boundless, which is another way of saying his self-awareness was not.

definition: To lay the foundation for a future offence.
example: He apologized with great sincerity, which is to say he was already planning the sequel.

definition: The echo of a platitude.
example: The speech received thunderous applause, which told you everything about the speech.

definition: The power by which a woman charms a lover and terrifies a husband.
example: Beauty is an asset that appreciates poorly and is taxed heavily by time.

definition: A person who talks when you wish him to listen.
example: He was an accomplished bore—a man who could empty a room with an anecdote.

definition: An apparatus with which we think that we think.
example: The brain is a magnificent instrument for generating the illusion of understanding.

definition: A woman with a fine prospect of happiness behind her.
example: She made a radiant bride—the future, of course, was another matter entirely.

definition: A more than commonly plain and unmistakable reminder that the affairs of this life are not of our own ordering.
example: The merger was, in retrospect, a calamity wearing a prospectus.

definition: An isolation ward for the dead.
example: They promoted him to a senior title—a kind of corporate cemetery for inconvenient talent.

definition: The period of human life intermediate between the idiocy of infancy and the folly of youth—two removes from the sin of manhood.
example: He spoke of his childhood with nostalgia, having apparently forgotten most of it.

definition: A state of mind produced by contemplation of a neighbor's uneasiness.
example: News of his rival's difficulties produced a warm, charitable comfort in him.

definition: Such an adjustment of conflicting interests as gives each adversary the satisfaction of thinking he has got what he ought not to have.
example: They reached a compromise—each party equally dissatisfied, which is to say it was fair.

definition: The inner voice that warns us somebody may be looking.
example: His conscience flared briefly, then was soothed by the absence of witnesses.

definition: A statesman enamored of existing evils, as distinguished from the Liberal, who wishes to replace them with others.
example: He called himself a conservative, meaning he preferred the evils he already knew.

definition: To seek another's approval of a course already decided on.
example: He consulted widely before doing exactly what he had always intended.

definition: An ingenious device for obtaining individual profit without individual responsibility.
example: The corporation expressed deep regret through its legal team and paid no further price.

definition: One who in a perilous emergency thinks with his legs.
example: He was not a coward so much as a man with an unusually rapid threat assessment.

definition: A blackguard whose faulty vision sees things as they are, not as they ought to be.
example: They called him a cynic; he considered this the most accurate compliment he had received.

definition: An ingenious substitute for the chain and whip of the slave-driver.
example: The mortgage was generous—only thirty years of voluntary servitude.

definition: The patriotic art of lying for one's country.
example: The diplomat crafted a statement of stunning diplomatic precision—every word technically defensible.

definition: A method of confirming others in their errors.
example: After three hours of productive discussion, everyone left more certain they had been right.

definition: A person of low taste, more interested in himself than in me.
example: He was, by unanimous consensus of all who knew him, a world-class egotist.

definition: The art of orally persuading fools that white is the color that it appears to be.
example: His eloquence was extraordinary—an ability to make the obvious sound profound.

definition: Belief without evidence in what is told by one who speaks without knowledge, of things without parallel.
example: He had faith in the projections—a quality that distinguished him from everyone who had read them.

definition: Conspicuously miserable.
example: She achieved everything she had wanted and was, at last, comprehensively famous.

definition: One who tells you better things about yourself than you deserve, thereby telling you nothing that is true.
example: He surrounded himself with excellent flatterers—the best that money could suborn.

definition: A ship big enough to carry two in fair weather, but only one in foul.
example: Their friendship survived everything life threw at it, until something actually went wrong.

definition: That period of time in which our affairs prosper, our friends are true, and our happiness is assured.
example: He invested heavily in the future, which is the only commodity sold exclusively on credit.

definition: An account of one's descent from an ancestor who did not particularly care to trace his own.
example: The genealogy was extensive and flattering—several convenient gaps had been tastefully omitted.

definition: The outward and visible sign of an inward fear.
example: Every organization has its ghosts—predecessors whose decisions haunt every meeting.

definition: An agreeable sensation arising from contemplating the misery of another.
example: He experienced a warm flush of happiness upon learning that his nemesis had been audited.

definition: An account, mostly false, of events, mostly unimportant, which are brought about by rulers, mostly knaves, and soldiers, mostly fools.
example: History judged him favorably—he had, after all, been the one to commission the history.

definition: Desire and expectation rolled into one.
example: He had tremendous hope, which is a polite way of saying he had done no research.

definition: The virtue which induces us to feed and lodge certain persons who are not in need of food and lodging.
example: They showed great hospitality to those who could repay it in kind.

definition: One who, professing virtues that he does not respect, secures the advantage of seeming to be what he despises.
example: He was no hypocrite—he simply had a broad and flexible definition of integrity.

definition: The state in which we must believe ourselves to be when confronted with the specious arguments of our opponents.
example: He confessed ignorance, which is a sophisticated way of declining to engage.

definition: A warehouse of facts, with poet and liar in joint ownership.
example: He had a powerful imagination—it was almost impossible to know which parts were true.

definition: Unable to perceive any promise of personal advantage from espousing either side of a controversy.
example: He was famously impartial, having been offered nothing to take a position.

definition: Wealth.
example: He repeated the offense with characteristic impunity.

definition: In matrimony, a similarity of tastes—particularly the taste for domination.
example: They cited incompatibility, which was accurate: both wanted to be the difficult one.

definition: A virtue which some persons mistake for a substitute for talent.
example: He compensated for genius with extraordinary industry—twelve hours a day of the wrong things.

definition: A commodity which in a more or less adulterated condition the State sells to the citizen as a reward for his allegiance.
example: He sought justice, which required only money, time, and a tolerance for disappointment.

definition: A group of twelve men who, having lied to the judge about their hearing and prejudices, have failed to fool him.
example: The jury deliberated for six hours before reaching the verdict the evidence had telegraphed in thirty minutes.

definition: One of the processes by which A acquires property for B.
example: He labored tirelessly for the good of the company, which was doing very well.

definition: Compatible with the will of a judge having jurisdiction.
example: The arrangement was entirely lawful; they had been most particular about that.

definition: One skilled in circumvention of the law.
example: He retained an excellent lawyer, which is to say someone fluent in creative compliance.

definition: One of imagination's most precious possessions.
example: They spoke movingly of liberty—their own, naturally; the concept had limits.

definition: A temporary insanity curable by marriage or by removal of the patient from the influences under which he incurred the disorder.
example: He was cured of love within six months, which was considered a speedy recovery.

definition: The state or condition of a community consisting of a master, a mistress, and two slaves, making in all, two.
example: They entered marriage with high hopes and realistic expectations of moderate disappointment.

definition: An attribute beloved of detected offenders.
example: He appealed eloquently for mercy, having been caught doing the thing he denied.

definition: The art of enhancing your charm by pretending not to be aware of it.
example: Her modesty was exquisite—a virtue so practiced it had become indistinguishable from performance.

definition: A blessing that is of no advantage to us excepting when we part with it.
example: He accumulated money with great discipline and spent it with great regret.

definition: Conforming to a local and mutable standard of right.
example: His conduct was entirely moral, provided one accepted the appropriate geographic and temporal coordinates.

definition: One whom we are commanded to love as ourselves, and who does all he can to make us disobedient.
example: His neighbor was a devoted Christian, which is to say he tested the commandments daily.

definition: A proponent of the doctrine that black is white.
example: They hired an optimist to present the quarterly results, which had the desired effect on morale.

definition: A minor form of despair, disguised as a virtue.
example: She practiced patience with grace—it was, by then, the only option remaining.

definition: Combustible rubbish ready to the torch of any one ambitious to illuminate his name.
example: He draped his ambition in patriotism, which lent it a respectable smell.

definition: In international affairs, a period of cheating between two periods of fighting.
example: The ceasefire was welcome; both sides needed time to regroup and prepare grievances.

definition: A lowly virtue whereby mediocrity achieves an inglorious success.
example: He succeeded through sheer perseverance—refusing to be deterred by ability.

definition: A route of many roads leading from nowhere to nothing.
example: He devoted twenty years to philosophy and emerged, at last, magnificently uncertain.

definition: One upon whom we set our hopes when ill and our dogs when well.
example: The physician was gifted, which the patient only discovered once he no longer needed one.

definition: The wisdom of a million fools in the diction of a dunce.
example: He concluded with a platitude, which was received with the nodding of heads and the vacancy of eyes.

definition: An eel in the fundamental mud upon which the superstructure of organized society is reared.
example: He was a seasoned politician—fluent in the art of meaning nothing at length.

definition: A strife of interests masquerading as a contest of principles.
example: They kept politics out of the room, which is a way of saying the money talked quietly.

definition: To ask that the laws of the universe be annulled in behalf of a single petitioner confessedly unworthy.
example: He prayed for a favorable outcome, outsourcing the problem to a department with no complaints line.

definition: A vagrant opinion without visible means of support.
example: His prejudice was thorough and categorical—he had not let evidence complicate it.

definition: To weigh probabilities in the scales of desire.
example: He reasoned carefully and arrived, inevitably, at the conclusion he had begun with.

definition: To seek a justification for a decision already made.
example: He promised to reconsider—a gesture of theatrical open-mindedness with no operational consequences.

definition: A daughter of Hope and Fear, explaining to Ignorance the nature of the Unknowable.
example: Religion and certainty share lodgings but are rarely introduced.

definition: A favorite weapon of the assassins of character.
example: The rumor spread quickly, assisted by those most loudly denying they had started it.

definition: A dead sinner revised and edited.
example: He achieved sainthood, which required only that his enemies outlive him.

definition: An obsolete kind of literary composition in which the vices and follies of the author's enemies were expounded with imperfect tenderness.
example: He called it satire; his subjects called it libel; posterity would call it journalism.

definition: Devoid of consideration for the selfishness of others.
example: He was called selfish by people who wanted what he had, which is a different thing.

definition: The one unpardonable sin against one's fellows.
example: His success was spectacular and, among his peers, profoundly unforgivable.

definition: A substitute, usually inadequate, for more substantial expressions of condolence.
example: She offered her deepest sympathy, which cost nothing and was priced accordingly.

definition: A formal inquiry designed to prove and put upon record the blameless characters of judges, advocates, and jurors.
example: The trial was conducted with the solemnity appropriate to a foregone conclusion.

definition: An ingenious compound of desirability and appearance.
example: He was committed to truth, particularly the kind that reflected well on him.

definition: A soldierly compound of vanity, duty, and the gambler's hope.
example: He was praised for his valor, a virtue that tends to look better in hindsight than in practice.

definition: The tribute of a fool to the worth of the nearest ass.
example: His vanity was so complete that criticism simply reorganized itself into confirmation.

definition: The instrument and symbol of a freeman's power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country.
example: He exercised his vote with the solemnity it deserved and the optimism it did not.

definition: A by-product of the arts of peace.
example: The war was conducted humanely, which meant both sides agreed on the paperwork.

definition: The salt with which the American humorist spoils his intellectual cookery by leaving it out.
example: He was known for his wit, most of which existed in his own estimation.

definition: That which discloses to the wise and disguises from the foolish their lack of understanding.
example: A fine education gave him the vocabulary to misunderstand things at a higher level.

definition: A member of a large and powerful tribe whose influence in human affairs has always been dominant and controlling.
example: He was not, technically, an idiot—he simply shared every characteristic feature of the category.

definition: Your irreverence toward my deity.
example: He was charged with impiety, a crime whose definition begins and ends with the accuser.

definition: Appointing your grandmother to office for the good of the party.
example: The appointment was meritocratic—they had interviewed all three relatives before deciding.

definition: A play representing life in another world, whose inhabitants have no speech but song and no motions but gestures.
example: He endured the opera with the suffering of a man who had paid to be there.

definition: A literary device whereby foolish readers think the worse of a book the better it is written.
example: He was accused of plagiarism—a charge that implied he had written something worth stealing.

definition: An erroneous appraisement.
example: His self-esteem was robust and entirely unsupported by external evidence.

definition: The grunt of the human hog attempting to slip its leash.
example: He dismissed her vocabulary as slang—a judgment that revealed more about him than her.

definition: Gentle reproof, as with a meat-axe.
example: The manager delivered an admonition so gentle that only the room fell quiet.

definition: A follower who has not yet obtained all that he expects to get.
example: His loyal adherents remained devoted, and would continue to do so until the inheritance cleared.

definition: A gastronome of the old school who preserves the simple tastes and adheres to the natural diet of the pre-pork period.
example: The committee consumed its weakest member in the manner of any well-run institution.

definition: A person who has the power of seeing that which is invisible to her patron—namely, that he is a blockhead.
example: She was not clairvoyant so much as observant, which produces identical results.

definition: A man who undertakes the management of our spiritual affairs as a method of bettering his temporal ones.
example: He took Holy Orders with genuine conviction and a shrewd eye for the living attached.

definition: Purchasing the barrel of whiskey that you do not need for the price of the cow that you cannot afford.
example: He practiced economy with great diligence, spending less on things he should not have had.

definition: A bondman's change from the tyranny of another to the despotism of himself.
example: He celebrated his emancipation from the firm by immediately replicating its worst tendencies alone.

definition: Exemption from the stress of authority in a beggarly half-dozen of restraint's infinite multitude of methods.
example: He was free in all the ways that did not matter and constrained in all the ways that did.

definition: One who makes heavy purchases of ingratitude, without materially affecting the price.
example: He was a generous benefactor, which is to say the ingratitude he received was world-class.

definition: The feeling of a prudent man for an enemy too formidable safely to be opposed.
example: He expressed profound contempt, which was his most sophisticated available response to feeling threatened.

definition: The only thing that the rich are willing for the poor to call theirs, and keep.
example: The new development promised distance from the city—an amenity priced accordingly.

definition: A person who can grasp the relation between things that are otherwise assumed to be unrelated.
example: He was called a genius after he was vindicated; before that, he was called difficult.

definition: A resumption of diplomatic relations and rectification of boundaries.
example: The divorce was amicable, which is the legal term for expensive and exhausting.
